note: A synthetic client (Slice 112 mock). Not a real company.
problem: We are a B2B SaaS company selling scheduling software to mid-sized clinics. Our monthly logo churn went from 4% to 7% in two quarters and we don't know why. Net revenue retention fell from 104% to 96% over the same period.

answers.common.decision: Whether next year's budget goes into a retention program or into new sales. The CEO decides at the board meeting.
answers.common.deadline: Board meeting in five weeks; a draft in three weeks.
answers.common.audience: The CEO and the board. They want the answer first and the few numbers that matter.
answers.common.materials: We have 850 customers paying on average $1,200 per month. 60% of churned accounts cited switching to a cheaper tool in exit surveys. Support tickets per account doubled after the March release.
answers.consulting.current-state: We added a discount offer at cancellation in Q2; the save rate is 15% of cancellation requests. Onboarding is fully self-serve. Churn is concentrated in clinics with fewer than 10 staff, which are 70% of churned logos.
answers.consulting.success: Get monthly churn back to 4% within two quarters without cutting list price.
answers.consulting.constraints: No more than two new hires, and engineering is committed through Q1.
